title: Tracking Food and Beverage Outlet Closures and Common Reasons for Closures
what_it_is: Tracking Food and Beverage Outlet Closures and Common Reasons for Closures

sections.label: F&B cessations and heritage businesses
sections.summary: Government does not track cessation breakdown; F&B entities rose 42% net from 2015 to 2025, and heritage businesses are supported, including New Bahru.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Government does not track the breakdown of cessations between standalone outlets, local chains and foreign chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The food services sector is highly competitive due to low barriers of entry, high product substitutability and rapidly shifting consumer preferences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2025, there has been a net increase of 42% in the number of food and beverages (F&B) entities, with formations outpacing cessations in most years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun, shared yesterday about our efforts to support heritage businesses under the Inter-agency Task Force for Heritage Businesses, Traditional Activities and Cultural Life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: An example is, of course, New Bahru, a creative cluster that blends heritage conservation with a curated mix of contemporary local F&B and lifestyle businesses.

sections.label: Proactive help for independent operators
sections.summary: Asked whether SME Centres could proactively help independent operators before they fold, the Government said it does not track those data and will consider the suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The last supplementary question is in relation to the independent operators, if they face difficulty, is it possible for SME Centres and maybe the consultants within these SME Centres to be more proactive to help these independent operators before they fold, especially some of those who are heritage independent operators?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We do not track those data, so we will take his suggestion into consideration.

sections.label: Food services productivity support programmes
sections.summary: The food services productivity report lets SMEs benchmark against peers, and the Food X Programme lets them outsource operationally difficult or expensive parts of operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Recently, we have the food services productivity report, which allows for SMEs to benchmark themselves with their peers to see what are the best practices, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Then, we have the Food X Programme, for example, that enables them to maybe outsource some of the more operationally difficult or expensive parts of their operations.
